maya_k: Heads up — I ran the new serializer + ONNX-PTQ build through the reranker eval harness and saw a consistent ~1.8% NDCG drop (short queries slice).

maya_k: Same model weights, only change was candidate serialization format (compact vs pretty) and we switched to the onnx-converted quantized runtime for smoke tests.

sanjay_r: hmm. do you have a minimal repro? can you paste the candidate text before/after serialization?

maya_k: quick example:
```
orig: \"How to configure SSO for ACME Corp?\"
serialized(compact): \"How to configure SSO for ACME Corp?\"
serialized(pretty): \"How to configure SSO for ACME Corp? \"  <-- trailing space only in pretty
```

maya_k: tokenizer picks up that trailing space differently in our prod tok vs the onnx runtime tok, which shifts token ids for short queries.

eli_h: trailing whitespace causing tokenization drift is flaky but plausible. ONNX runtime might be using different encoding (utf-8 normalization?) or our preprocess strip flag got toggled.

eli_h: try normalizing with:
```python
text = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', text).rstrip()
```

alex_do: also worth checking if prefix cache or kv pack alignment changed — a small token shift at start can cascade. did you evaluate top1 vs top5?

maya_k: top1 loss is larger (2.4%) than top5 (0.6%). suggests ranker sensitivity to first tokens.

rachel_p: how big is the eval set? maybe sampling noise.

maya_k: full golden holdout (25k queries). signal is outside a normal CI window. repeated 3 runs, consistent.

sanjay_r: can you run a quick A/B: same candidate pool but force serializer=pretty vs compact and run the scoring with FP16 CPU runtime (no ONNX) to isolate serializer vs runtime?

maya_k: doing that now. ETA ~20m.

ci-bot: Deploy test #rkr-3487 failed: rerank-eval-smoke (serializer-change) — job logs: https://ci.example/redwood/runs/3487

alex_do: if serializer only, I suspect whitespace/linebreak normalization. we had a prior bug where multi-sentence docs got an extra newline between sentences when compact was used.

eli_h: small experiment idea: diff token IDs between pre and post for the same candidate set. script:
```bash
python -c \"from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tok.json'); print(t.encode('How to configure SSO for ACME Corp?'))\"
```

maya_k: sanjay confirmed: compact serializer removed a trailing NBSP in ~8% of candidates. that maps to different subtokenization for short queries.

sanjay_r: ok that's the smoking gun. NBSP -> regular space -> different bpe split. PTQ + ONNX amplifies the small score deltas.

rachel_p: mitigation options: 1) upstream serializer normalize NBSP->space; 2) eval harness add normalization step so offline and online match; 3) add a dataset slice to catch this in pre-commit.

alex_do: add (1) and (2) immediately. we should also add a small regression test in rankbench that asserts token id parity for a sample set.

eli_h: pushing a tiny patch to serializer to NFKC + replace('\\u00A0',' ') and rerun.

maya_k: thanks — re-run results: NDCG delta back to baseline within noise (0.2%).

maya_k: filing follow-ups:
- maya_k: ticket RINF-7234 normalize serializer output and add token-parity test
- maya_k: ticket RINF-7235 add eval harness preproc normalization flag

rachel_p: please add a note in the eval runbook about tokenizer parity checks.

sanjay_r: will add a one-liner to the onboarding checklist: \"verify serialization & tokenizer parity across conversion paths\".

ci-bot: Created issue RINF-7234 and RINF-7235 in tracker.

alex_do: nice catch, @maya_k. small format differences are sneaky. :thumbsup:
